$comment: AUTHORITY for the Xynolog event bus: channels, their payloads, and the request/reply operations. Every SDK's channel table is generated from this file — edit here, then run `make generate` in sdk, whose consumer-owned generator writes every SDK's. Payload schemas themselves live in the OpenAPI components; `validate` names the one a channel carries on the wire. A channel's delivery class (positioned, correlated or passing: what a subscriber is promised when its stream drops) is not stated here: the consumer-owned generator derives it from `operations`, `audience` and which channels are events of the record. Its prose is plain text in no language's shape, which each generator lays out for its own language: a docs entry is `lead`, the blocks written before the entry ("" where the listing breaks, a `section`, a `comment`, or a `doc` of the entry itself), and `trailing`, a note after it on its line; prose is a list of paragraphs, each a text or a list of `items`. The reader in reader/ holds it to that.

Client-local: a delegated job went silent past its deadline (no progress, no completion, no job:fail). Emitted by mark-state-unit so the outcome-notification layer can tell the user; a real job failure arrives as job:fail instead and never produces this.

Client-local UI notifications for annotation command failures, emitted by the awaiting catch (mark-state-unit), which inherently knows whose command failed on which resource. Distinct from the `mark:create-failed` / `mark:delete-failed` wire replies above: those are Bus.request correlation plumbing (CommandError, matched by correlationId, delivered to the requesting client) and are NOT for UI consumption — subscribing to them raw toasts the requester twice.

Same pattern for bind body updates initiated by callers that cannot toast directly (e.g. ReferenceEntry's unlink); awaiting callers with their own toast surface (the reference wizard) surface failures themselves instead.

lead.section: WEAVE FLOW — graph projection progress, pushed by the Weaver, not polled

doc: Emitted by the Weaver after applying an event (or a batch's last event) for a resource to the graph. `sequenceNumber` is the resource-stream sequence of the last applied event. Folded by the Librarian's `WeaveProgress` into a process-local applied map that its `when_applied` barrier awaits. The Weaver runs as its own process, so the signal reaches the fold over the bus.

comment: Signal — the vector projection's per-resource decision report: emitted by the Smelter after indexing a resource's content ('indexed') or after deciding not to ('skipped', with a `reason` naming the decline: 'no-extractor', 'empty', or one of the PDF decline classes). Keyed by the checksum of the bytes inspected — "settled at C" is read-your-writes for exactly that content. NEVER emitted on transient failures: an error is not a decision. Consumed by the process-local `SmeltProgress` folds behind the gather and anchored-text barriers. This is the Smelter's single outbound signal.

Command — rebuild the graph projection from the event log (full when resourceId is absent, one resource when present). Served by the Weaver over the bus: a direct `rebuildAll()`/`rebuildResource()` call cannot reach a Weaver running in its own container. Correlated request/reply via the BUS_OPERATIONS registry.

Command — rebuild anchored-text artifacts by re-running extraction (every geometry-capable resource when resourceId is absent, one when present). Served by the Smelter, serialized, never destructive, and with ZERO embedding calls — only the derived map is re-made. Correlated request/reply via BUS_OPERATIONS.

doc: Written by the `/bus/subscribe` handler when a scoped entry's `lastEventId` cannot be honoured — the watermark is unparseable or names another scope, the record no longer holds the events after it, or the record could not be read. The client falls back to invalidating what it caches for that scope and re-reading it.

eventName: Any valid channel name on the EventBus — `keyof EventMap`, the root channel type. Two subsets matter, and confusing them is a silent-failure trap:

items: `EmittableChannel` (below) — channels with a non-null `CHANNEL_SCHEMAS` entry; what you EMIT (the `/bus/emit` gateway validates the payload).
`BridgedChannel` (`bridged-channels.ts`) — the transport fan-in set; the only channels a client can SUBSCRIBE to over a concrete transport.

eventName: Request/reply (`Bus.request`) emits on an `EmittableChannel` and subscribes on `BridgedChannel` replies. A reply channel that is a valid `EventName` but NOT in `BRIDGED_CHANNELS` is never delivered → the request times out with no compile or runtime error. `Bus.request` therefore takes no reply channels: it looks them up in `BUS_OPERATIONS`, from which `BRIDGED_CHANNELS` derives.
enrichedEvents: Channels whose published event carries the annotation as it stands in the view — the registry's `enriched` flag, generated so the flag and the code that acts on it cannot disagree.

The enricher switches on THIS list: a flag with no case fails to compile rather than silently never attaching, which consumers cannot detect because `annotation` is optional and their absent-branch is indistinguishable from a genuine decline.
Typed `PersistedEventType`, not `EventName`: the validator already allows the flag only on a stored event, so this makes enriched ⊆ persisted a compile-time fact rather than a convention.
channelSchemas: Authoritative map from bus channel to OpenAPI schema name.
Every `EventName` must appear. The `satisfies` clause below enforces completeness at compile time — adding a channel to `EventMap` without adding an entry here is a build error.

items: `null`: no single-schema validation. Used for branded `StoredEvent` wrappers, `void` UI signals, and inline wrapper types (e.g. `{ response: T }`). These are not validated by `/bus/emit`.

channelSchemas: The gateway's `/bus/emit` route validates against the same registry entries. Consumers can use this map for client-side pre-flight validation before emitting.
emittableChannel: Channels where `/bus/emit` validates the payload (non-null schema).

doc: Explicitly LOCAL-ONLY: these channels never cross the signal plane — UI signals, event-log appends, and single-process relays. Membership is a DECISION, not a default: a channel absent from every class (operations, outboundCommands, bridgedBroadcasts, here) refuses to generate. There is no fallthrough: one would silently classify a wire channel such as `job:queued` as in-process and starve every worker.
How a wire-crossing channel behaves. An OPERATION's channels are absent: their kind follows from `operations`, and restating a derivable fact is a mirror with nothing to gate it.
`kind`, not `shape` — `channels[]` entries already use `shape` for the PAYLOAD shape, and two facts under one key in one file is the disease this taxonomy exists to cure.

items: command — no reply pair; a directive for whichever single handler owns it
event — a fact announced after it happened; consumers react, nobody replies

doc: WHO receives a wire-crossing channel — independent of `kind` and of `recorded`. An OPERATION's channels are absent: a request reaches the one service that answers it, and a reply is correlated-addressed to its owner.

items: everyone — every full client subscribes, with every operation's reply channels (derives BRIDGED_CHANNELS)
scoped — delivered to clients that joined the frame's RESOURCE scope (derives RESOURCE_SCOPED_CHANNELS)
declared — only clients whose manifest names it: workers, sidecars, and the gateway's own handlers

doc: Does emitting this channel CHANGE the knowledge base, or only ask it something?

A WRITE is an act: it appends to the event log, or it enqueues or transitions durable work the log will later cite. A READ answers from state that already exists and leaves nothing behind — every `browse:*` request, and the three lookups that merely resolve a token or a summary.

The domain is exactly the EMITTABLE set: an operation's request, or a `kind: command`. Inbound replies, broadcast events and in-process UI signals are absent because nobody emits them at the gateway, so the question does not arise. Every emittable channel names one side or the other and the generator refuses — there is no default.

The gateway reads this to decide when the record learns a principal's name: a `_userId` stamp is NOT the test, because a read carries one too. Someone who signs in and only browses is never named, and the profile publish rate is the WRITE rate rather than the emit rate — orders of magnitude apart.

trace.meaning: The field of a relayed frame's payload that carries the trace the frame was published under: a client/types/TraceCarrier.json: W3C's `traceparent` and, when it has one, `tracestate`. A frame the gateway relays over the stream has no headers of its own, so the gateway writes the field on its payload, and a receiver takes it off before the payload is delivered and continues the trace from it. No payload schema declares it, and no subscriber sees it. An emit carries its trace in its request's `traceparent` header, and its payload carries no such field.

stamps.meaning: The members of an emitted payload that name who emitted it, which the gateway writes on every payload `POST /bus/emit` takes, after its schema has held it and in place of anything the emitter put there. `emitter` holds the DID the gateway names the emitter by (principals/cases.json). `roles` holds the roles of the emitter's token, and is written only when the token holds any: a payload whose emitter's token holds none carries no such member. A failure frame the gateway delivers itself carries neither.
